one_sentence_story: When Stanford preschoolers watched an adult hit an inflatable Bobo clown with a wooden mallet for ten minutes, they walked into the next room and copied every strike and catchphrase with zero reward — proving humans learn scripts simply by watching.
so_what_for_you: Audit what you model when frustrated: children and teammates absorb how you act under stress far faster than anything you lecture them to do.

jargon_map.plain: acquiring a brand-new behavior simply by watching someone else perform it
jargon_map.analogy: like learning how to fold a paper airplane by watching across the table

jargon_map.plain: mistaken belief that watching or venting anger empties out inner frustration
jargon_map.analogy: like thinking pouring fuel on a stove cools the kitchen

jargon_map.plain: scoring behavior blindly every five seconds from behind mirrored glass
jargon_map.analogy: like referees tallying plays without the players seeing them

jargon_map.plain: silently storing a watched skill even before choosing to act it out
jargon_map.analogy: like knowing all the words to a song you've never sung out loud

jargon_map.plain: lowering group tension by visibly demonstrating quiet, constructive action
jargon_map.analogy: like one calm pilot steadying the whole cockpit voice
